questions.stem: Why must image size and actual size be in the same units before calculating magnification?

options.text: Different units make the microscope produce blurry images
Magnification is a ratio with no units, so both measurements must use the same units to give a correct value
The formula only works with millimetres
Different units are needed for different types of microscope

questions.explanation: Magnification is a unitless ratio (image size divided by actual size). For the ratio to be meaningful, both measurements must be in the same units so the units cancel out.
